quality_assessment: Chapter contains CRITICAL errors in built-in alias definitions that will cause broken hyperlinks for users. The kitty and grep+ aliases have completely wrong URL schemes. The file alias is missing the {host} variable. These errors make the chapter actively harmful as users will copy non-functional formats. Otherwise, the chapter structure and coverage are excellent.

issues.description: The 'kitty' alias format is completely wrong - uses non-existent 'kitty+kitten://' scheme instead of 'file://' with fragment
issues.fix_suggestion:
Replace line 36 with: | `kitty` | `file://{host}{path}#{line}` |

The kitty alias uses RFC 8089 file:// scheme with a fragment identifier (#line) for line numbers, NOT a custom 'kitty+kitten://' scheme.

issues.description: The 'grep+' alias format is completely wrong - uses non-existent 'x-grepapp://' scheme instead of 'grep+://'
issues.fix_suggestion:
Replace line 37 with: | `grep+` | `grep+://{path}:{line}` |

The grep+ alias uses a simple 'grep+://' scheme, NOT 'x-grepapp://' with query parameters.

issues.description: The 'file' alias format is incomplete - missing {host} variable
issues.fix_suggestion:
Replace line 29 with: | `file` | `file://{host}{path}` |

The file alias always includes the {host} variable. This differs from the 'default' alias which only includes {host} on Unix platforms.

issues.description: Example comment is misleading - suggests kitty opens in 'built-in editor' but it uses file:// scheme
issues.current_content:
# Open results in Kitty's built-in editor
rg --hyperlink-format kitty pattern
issues.should_be:
# Open results using kitty's file:// handler (with line number fragment)
rg --hyperlink-format kitty pattern
issues.fix_suggestion: Replace line 201 comment to accurately describe that kitty uses RFC 8089 file:// scheme with fragment identifier for line numbers, not a special editor protocol

issues.description: IntelliJ, Sublime, and Neovim examples suggest these are viable formats but may not work without URL scheme registration
issues.current_content:
# IntelliJ/PyCharm/WebStorm (community format)
rg --hyperlink-format 'idea://open?file={path}&line={line}' pattern

# Sublime Text (community format)
rg --hyperlink-format 'subl://open?url=file://{path}&line={line}' pattern

# Neovim remote (community format)
rg --hyperlink-format 'nvim://edit/{path}:+{line}' pattern
issues.should_be: Add stronger warning that these are untested community formats requiring manual URL scheme registration
issues.fix_suggestion: Add prominent note before line 153: 'WARNING: These are community-suggested formats and may require custom URL scheme handlers to be registered with your OS. They are not built into ripgrep or guaranteed to work.'
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/hyperlink/aliases.rs (no built-in aliases exist for these editors)

issues.description: The difference between 'file' and 'default' aliases could be clearer
issues.current_content:
**The `default` alias** is platform-aware and expands differently per platform:
- Unix/Linux/macOS: `file://{host}{path}` (includes hostname)
- Windows: `file://{path}` (omits hostname for compatibility)

The default alias follows RFC 8089 file:// URI specification and is the recommended choice for general use.
issues.should_be: Add comparison: 'Note: The `file` alias ALWAYS includes {host}, while `default` only includes it on Unix platforms. Use `default` for maximum cross-platform compatibility.'
issues.fix_suggestion: After line 44, add: 'The `file` alias differs from `default` by always including the hostname, even on Windows. Use `default` for cross-platform compatibility.'
